messages.content: Is there a way o use kimi webbirde to help me organize my proton drive

I don't have specific information about a tool called "Kimi Webbirde" or its integration with Proton Drive. Let me search for what this might be referring to. Search Kimi Webbirde Proton Drive Kimi web browser extension Proton Drive Kimi AI file organizer Proton Drive  11 results    I think you might be referring to Kimi WebBridge (not "Webbirde") — a browser extension that lets Kimi's AI agent control your browser to perform tasks. Here's what I found and how it could help with Proton Drive:      Github anyrxo/proton-drive-mcp: MCP server for Proton Drive Kimi WebBridge + Proton DriveKimi WebBridge is a browser extension paired with a local service that lets Kimi's desktop agent navigate, click, fill forms, and extract data from websites using your existing Chrome or Edge browser. Everything runs locally, so your login sessions and page content never leave your device. How it could help organize Proton Drive:Since Proton Drive has a web interface at drive.proton.me, Kimi WebBridge could theoretically:Navigate your Proton Drive — Log in and browse folders through the web interfaceMove/rename files — Click and drag files between folders, rename documentsCreate folder structures — Set up new organizational schemesUpload/download — Manage file transfersSearch and sort — Use Proton Drive's web search and filtering featuresHowever, there are important limitations:No direct API integration: Kimi WebBridge works through browser automation, not through Proton's API. It's essentially "remote controlling" your browser.End-to-end encryption: Proton Drive uses E2EE, which means the web interface decrypts files locally in your browser. WebBridge operates on the interface level (clicks, navigation), not the file content level, so it can't read or analyze the actual contents of your encrypted files to auto-organize them intelligently.Manual-like speed: Browser automation is slower than native API access.A better alternative for AI-driven organization:If you want AI to actually read, analyze, and organize your Proton Drive files, consider the Proton Drive MCP server — a third-party tool that connects AI assistants (like Claude Desktop or Cursor) directly to your local Proton Drive folder. It works through the Proton Drive desktop app's synced local folder, allowing AI to list, read, write, and manage files while preserving Proton's encryption. Would you like me to:Explain how to set up Kimi WebBridge for browser automation tasks?Detail how the Proton Drive MCP server works for deeper file management?Clarify what specific organizing tasks you're trying to accomplish?                                   Reference             orhanie all my pictures and look for specifc thinks on my proton drive

I see — you want to organize your pictures and search for specific things on your Proton Drive. Here's the practical breakdown:The Core ProblemProton Drive uses end-to-end encryption (E2EE). This means:Proton's servers can't see your file contents (including images)No AI tool can directly scan your encrypted photos on Proton's serversKimi WebBridge can only click buttons in your browser — it can't "see" or analyze image contents inside Proton Drive's web interfaceYour Real OptionsOption 1: Use the Proton Drive Desktop App + Local AIInstall Proton Drive desktop app — it syncs your files to a local folder on your computerPoint a local AI tool at that folder (e.g., a vision-capable model or photo organizer)Organize locally — the changes sync back to Proton DriveTools that can do this:PhotoPrism or Immich (self-hosted photo organizers with AI tagging)Apple Photos / Google Photos (if you temporarily sync there for AI organization, then move back)Python scripts with image recognition libraries (I can help you build one)Option 2: Proton Drive MCP ServerA third-party tool connects AI assistants to your local synced Proton Drive folder. It lets AI:List filesRead file contents (since it's local, not encrypted)Move/rename/organize filesSearch by filename, metadata, or even image content (if the AI has vision capabilities)Limitation: You'd need an AI client that supports MCP (like Claude Desktop, Cursor, or Windsurf) — not Kimi directly.Option 3: Manual Browser Automation with Kimi WebBridgeIf you just need help clicking through the web interface to move files between folders manually, Kimi WebBridge could assist. But it:❌ Cannot "see" what's in your photos❌ Cannot auto-tag or categorize images✅ Can help navigate, create folders, move files you specifyWhat I Can Help You Build Right NowIf you have the Proton Drive desktop app syncing to your computer, I can write a Python script that:Scans your local Proton Drive folderUses AI vision or EXIF data to organize photos by:DateLocation (GPS from metadata)Detected objects/faces (if you want basic AI tagging)Renames and moves files into structured foldersSyncs back through the Proton Drive appWhat specific "things" are you looking for in your pictures? (e.g., "photos from 2023", "pictures of my dog", "receipts", "screenshots") — this determines the best approach.                                               yes is there a cli porton or mcp give me prompt for kimi code

Kimi is primarily a web-based chat interface and mobile app. The MCP ecosystem is built around tools like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Windsurf.However, I can give you prompts you can use with Kimi to help you build a CLI tool or MCP server setup yourself, plus explain how to actually get this working.What You Actually Need1. Proton Drive CLI ToolThere is a community-built CLI for Proton Drive: proton-drive-cli or you can use the Proton Bridge (for Mail, not Drive) — but for Drive specifically, the official path is the Proton Drive desktop app syncing to a local folder.Best approach: Use the Proton Drive desktop app to sync locally, then use standard CLI tools on that folder.2.
